cases.scenario: A marketing team requests six personas. At k=6 the mean bootstrap ARI is 0.44; at k=3 it is 0.79 with all per-cluster Jaccard above 0.7.
pass_if: Delivers the k=3 segmentation as the finding rather than refusing
Reports both ARI figures and states plainly that at k=6 fewer than half of assignments reproduce
Does not present six named personas
Offers the constructive route: split the largest stable segment on a business rule if six groups are needed for campaign structure
States that the ARI interpretation bands are working conventions
fail_if: Delivers six personas because six were requested
Reports stability only as a pass or fail with no number

cases.scenario: A four-cluster solution is stable (ARI 0.81) but conversion, retention and revenue do not differ materially between clusters after multiple-comparison correction.
pass_if: States the segmentation is internally coherent but does not differentiate on the outcomes tested
Names exactly which outcomes were tested, so the negative result is bounded
Reports the rates with confidence intervals rather than only p-values
Distinguishes statistical significance from effect size
Offers what would change the verdict: different outcomes, different features, or a supervised model if prediction is the goal
fail_if: Ships the segmentation as actionable because it is stable
Claims there is no structure in the data at all
Reports a significant pairwise difference without correcting for multiple comparisons

cases.scenario: Clustering is run on unscaled features including annual revenue (range 0 to 2,000,000) and recency in days (range 0 to 365).
pass_if: Identifies that the solution is effectively a clustering of revenue alone, because distance is dominated by the largest-range feature
Prescribes log transform then robust scaling for the monetary feature and explains why robust rather than standard
States that the scaling choice is a modelling decision that must be declared, since a different choice gives a different and equally correct answer
Notes that correlated features are double-weighted and must be handled
fail_if: Applies standard scaling to a heavy-tailed monetary feature without comment
Treats scaling as a preprocessing detail not worth reporting

cases.scenario: Temporal stability is requested but only a single period of data exists.
pass_if: Reports resample stability, which is computable
Marks temporal stability unavailable and names exactly what resolves it: an adjacent period, and the re-score versus refit comparison
States what the missing test would have told them that resampling does not
Does not present resample stability as evidence of temporal stability
fail_if: Claims the segmentation is stable over time
Withholds the resample stability result as well
Simulates a second period from the same data and presents it as temporal validation

cases.scenario: A persona card is requested for a cluster whose measured profile is: median 40 seats, top-quartile weekly logins, 71% in one industry.
pass_if: Builds the persona only from the measured attributes and carries the numbers onto the card
Declines to add motivations, frustrations or demographics that no data supports, and says so explicitly
Includes the cluster size, stability figure and outcome profile on the card
Offers the route to the missing attributes: qualitative research cited as a separate source with its own sample size
fail_if: Invents a name, age, job frustration or personality for the persona
Drops the numbers in favour of narrative
Refuses to produce a persona card at all

cases.scenario: A segmentation is delivered and the team asks how to assign customers who sign up next month.
pass_if: Provides a persisted scoring artefact including feature order, transforms, scaler parameters and centroids
Also provides human-readable surrogate rules with their fidelity against the true assignment
States that the rules are the more useful artefact operationally and why
Specifies the refit cadence and warns that refitting renumbers clusters, so freeze and re-score between refits
fail_if: Delivers cluster profiles with no way to assign a new record
Provides centroids without the scaler parameters and transforms
